statement: A Riccati equation in the narrowest sense is a first-order ordinary differential equation that is quadratic in the unknown function, having the form y'(x) = q_0(x) + q_1(x) y(x) + q_2(x) y^2(x) where q_0(x) != 0 and q_2(x) != 0. The supplied sources contain no derivation of this equation (such as via backward recursion or quadratic form differentiation), defining it as an object directly.

properties.why: If q_0(x) = 0, the equation reduces to y'(x) = q_1(x) y(x) + q_2(x) y^2(x)
If q_2(x) = 0, the quadratic term vanishes, yielding y'(x) = q_0(x) + q_1(x) y(x)

properties.property: Conversion to a second-order linear ODE
properties.why: Using substitutions v = y q_2 and u' = -u v transforms the equation into u'' - R(x) u' + S(x) u = 0, where S = q_0 q_2 and R = q_1 + q_2'/q_2

properties.property: Solvability by quadrature given a particular solution
properties.why: Given a known particular solution y_1, substituting y = y_1 + 1/z yields the linear ODE z' + (q_1 + 2 q_2 y_1) z = -q_2

properties.property: Painlevé property in the complex plane
properties.why: Among first-order complex rational ODEs dw/dz = P(w, z)/Q(w, z), the Riccati equation dw/dz = A_0(z) + A_1(z) w + A_2(z) w^2 is the only one of Painlevé type

assumptions.breaks_when: q_0(x) = 0, which reduces the Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation
q_2(x) = 0, which reduces the equation to a first-order linear ODE
q_2(x) fails to be differentiable or vanishes, preventing transformation into the standard form v' = S(x) + R(x)v + v^2 and linear ODE

failure_modes.cause: The quadratic term vanishes, causing degeneration into a linear ODE
The zeroth-order term vanishes, causing degeneration into a Bernoulli ODE

failure_modes.mode: Division by zero in linearizing substitution
failure_modes.cause: The formula y = -u' / (q_2 u) or y = v / q_2 encounters a zero denominator

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so riccati_equation is recorded as a definition
